methods.label: Find the sum and product of the lengths
methods.explanation:
The two lengths already have a known sum: \(AT+TB=p\). We therefore seek their product, since numbers \(r\) and \(s\) are the roots of
\[
(x-r)(x-s)=x^2-(r+s)x+rs=0.
\]
The stated construction presupposes \(p>0\) and \(0\le q\le p/2\).

First suppose \(0<q<p/2\), and let \(u=MT\). Because the arc has center \(R\) and radius \(p/2\), we have \(RT=p/2\). The Pythagorean theorem in right triangle \(RMT\) gives
\[
u^2+q^2=\frac{p^2}{4}.
\]
Since \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\), the lengths \(AT\) and \(TB\) are \(p/2-u\) and \(p/2+u\), in some order. Thus
\[
AT\cdot TB
=\left(\frac p2-u\right)\left(\frac p2+u\right)
=\frac{p^2}{4}-u^2=q^2.
\]
Their sum and product therefore give \(x^2-px+q^2=0\).

At \(q=p/2\), the arc is tangent to \(AB\) at \(M\), so both lengths equal \(p/2\); the equation becomes \((x-p/2)^2=0\). At \(q=0\), the intersections are the endpoints, giving lengths \(0\) and \(p\), and the equation becomes \(x(x-p)=0\). If \(q>p/2\), the arc cannot meet \(AB\). Thus whenever the stated construction exists, the required equation is \(\boxed{x^2-px+q^2=0}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
